card.name: Linking words joining two interacting items
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as with, and, to, through or an arrow, placed right after one item and before its partner. Most often in drug interaction text where one drug is paired with another.

modes.label: Drug pairing
modes.description: The word 'with' or 'and' between two co-administered drugs or doses.
modes.example: Co-administration of multiple doses of 10 mg of verapamil<< with>> 80 mg simvastatin

modes.label: Everyday relation words
modes.description: A preposition after a verb that expects a partner or object, in general prose.
modes.example: I was incredibly proud of how easily they chatted<< with>> the senior citizens because of their genuine interest

card.writes: It suppresses words meaning 'with' or 'paired', mostly in Chinese and Japanese, so it seems to lessen further pairing words.
card.plain: It fires on the small word that links one drug or thing to the one it is combined or interacting with.
